claim_text: After alumni and student groups asked Dartmouth in April 2026 to remove Leon Black's name from the Black Family Visual Arts Center, the board of trustees formed an ad hoc naming-policy committee at its June 11-14 meeting; no decision on the name had been reported as of September 24, 2026.

On February 18, 2026 a majority of Hasty Pudding Theatricals' current company petitioned for Andrew Farkas's resignation as chair of the Hasty Pudding Institute over his documented ties to Epstein; no resignation had been reported as of September 24, 2026.

On March 3, 2026 Sen. Mike Crapo objected to Sen. Ron Wyden's unanimous-consent request to pass the Produce Epstein Treasury Records Act, which would compel Treasury to provide Epstein-related bank records to Congress.

Sen. Ron Wyden wrote to Leon Black on March 20, 2026 stating that DOJ records put Black's payments to Epstein at $170 million and appear to show hush-money payments routed through Epstein and surveillance of women; Black's representative said the letter had no legitimate legislative purpose.
On June 4, 2026 Sen. Ron Wyden referred findings from his Senate Finance investigation of Leon Black's payments to Epstein to House Oversight Chairman James Comer and Ranking Member Robert Garcia.

Sen. Ron Wyden said on March 18, 2026 that Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche intervened to stop DEA from giving the Senate Finance Committee an unredacted 2015 drug-task-force memo describing an investigation of Epstein and 14 unnamed others; Blanche called the account fabricated and said the report is available unredacted to members of Congress in DOJ's reading room.
